title: Transformers, LLMs, and Modern AI Systems
description: Attention, the transformer, pretraining, and the systems around a large model. LLMs are a destination, not lesson one.

sourceReferences.title: Stanford CS224N Natural Language Processing with Deep Learning
sourceReferences.notes: Even when the calendar compresses RNNs, attention is taught as a solution to sequence-model limits. Pretraining, then adaptation, then RAG/tools/evaluation. Assumes CS229-level foundations.

concepts.name: Sequence transduction
concepts.summary: Map one sequence onto another without a fixed window.
objectives: State sequence transduction as mapping one sequence onto another without a fixed window
Name what a fixed-window model cannot see that a longer mixer can

concepts.name: Tokenization
concepts.summary: The discrete units a model actually sees.
objectives: Describe tokenization as the discrete units a model actually sees
Predict how a bad split changes what 'word' the model can attend to

concepts.name: Attention
concepts.summary: QKV as a content-addressable lookup, and why it scales.
objectives: Score keys with a query and mix the values as a content-addressable lookup
State why naive all-pairs scoring costs the square of the length

concepts.name: Queries, keys, and values
concepts.summary: Three roles for the same tokens.
objectives: Give the same tokens three roles: query, key, and value
Predict what breaks if you mix values with scores that were not computed from keys

concepts.name: Self-attention
concepts.summary: Every position looking at every other position in the same sequence.
objectives: Let every position look at every other position in the same sequence
Trace one token's update as a weighted mix of the other tokens

concepts.name: Multi-head attention
concepts.summary: Several lookups in parallel, each free to specialize.
objectives: Run several lookups in parallel so heads can specialize
Predict a job one head can take that a single average would smear

concepts.name: Positional information
concepts.summary: Attention has no order unless you give it one.
objectives: Add order because attention has none of its own
Predict what a permutation of tokens does to an unpositioned mixer

concepts.name: The transformer block
concepts.summary: Attention, residual, normalization, feed-forward — stacked.
objectives: Stack attention, residual, normalization, and feed-forward as one block
Name what the residual path preserves that a bare stack would lose

concepts.name: Encoder, decoder, decoder-only
concepts.summary: Three layouts for three jobs.
objectives: Choose encoder, decoder, or decoder-only for the job
Predict which layout can see the future of the output and which must not

concepts.name: Language-model objectives
concepts.summary: Next-token prediction as the pretraining game.
objectives: Train by predicting the next token from the past
State why that objective produces a useful representation you can later adapt

concepts.name: Pretraining
concepts.summary: A lot of unlabeled text, one objective, a representation you will reuse.
objectives: Run one objective on a lot of unlabeled text to get a reusable representation
Contrast pretraining with the narrower job you will later fine-tune for

concepts.name: Scale as a design choice
concepts.summary: Parameters, data, and compute as coupled knobs.
objectives: Treat parameters, data, and compute as coupled knobs, not independent bragging rights
Predict what happens if you grow one knob and starve the others

concepts.name: Fine-tuning
concepts.summary: Continuing training on a narrower distribution.
objectives: Continue training on a narrower distribution without throwing the representation away
Diagnose a fine-tune that forgets the general skill you paid to pretrain

concepts.name: Parameter-efficient adaptation
concepts.summary: Changing a small adapter instead of every weight.
objectives: Change a small adapter instead of every weight
Compare the cost and flexibility of an adapter with full fine-tuning

concepts.name: Prompting
concepts.summary: Inference-time control written in the model's own language.
objectives: Control the model at inference time in its own language
Predict what a prompt can and cannot change that a weight update can

concepts.name: Preference tuning
concepts.summary: SFT, then a preference signal, then the arguments about reward.
objectives: Follow supervised fine-tune with a preference signal, then argue about the reward
Distinguish next-token likelihood from a preference that prefers one completion

concepts.name: Inference versus training
concepts.summary: The forward pass you serve, without the backward pass you trained.
objectives: Serve the forward pass without the backward pass you trained
Name a cost that exists at generate time that did not dominate training

concepts.name: Context windows
concepts.summary: How much past the model can attend to, and what that costs.
objectives: State how much past the model can attend to, and what that costs
Predict what falls out of a window that is shorter than the document

concepts.name: The KV cache
concepts.summary: Remembering keys and values so you do not recompute the past.
objectives: Remember past keys and values so you do not recompute the prefix
Explain why a causal mask makes that cache valid while generating

concepts.name: Retrieval-augmented generation
concepts.summary: Looking something up instead of hoping the weights remember.
objectives: Look something up instead of hoping the weights remember
Predict a failure when retrieval is wrong but the continuation is fluent

concepts.name: Tool use and agents
concepts.summary: A model that calls a tool, reads the result, and continues.
objectives: Let the model call a tool, read the result, and continue
Distinguish a tool loop from a single forward pass that only emits text

concepts.name: Evaluating generative models
concepts.summary: Benchmarks, contamination, and the thing a leaderboard cannot see.
objectives: Evaluate a generative model with more than a leaderboard number
Name contamination and the thing a benchmark cannot see

concepts.name: Failure modes
concepts.summary: What breaks: reasoning, attribution, calibration, incentives.
objectives: Name reasoning, attribution, calibration, and incentive failures as different breaks
Diagnose a fluent answer that fails for a reason other than 'the model is dumb'

concepts.name: Hallucination as calibration
concepts.summary: A fluent continuation that is not a retrieved fact.
objectives: Treat hallucination as a fluent continuation that is not a retrieved fact
Predict why next-token training does not punish a confident falsehood by itself

concepts.name: Sparse and linear attention bets
concepts.summary: Not every pair of tokens has to meet.
objectives: Skip pairs of tokens that do not need to meet
Compare a sparse or linear attention bet with full all-pairs scoring
